summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book, the narrator and Arthur face Finch and his boss, Steve, at a picnic table. Steve threatens to expose everything, including the narrator's involvement, if they don't hear from his contact, and offers a disappearance deal. The narrator rejects the offer, and the two leave. The narrator knocks out Finch and his boss by throwing a branch, but then sees a red laser sight on his chest, suggesting a new threat.
one_line: The narrator rejects a threatening offer from Steve and Finch at a picnic area, knocks both men out with a thrown branch, then spots a red laser sight on his chest.
key_facts: Steve claims he has a contact on the outside who knows everything, including about running into Mr. Finch, and that if he does not hear from them, everything will go public.
Steve tells the narrator that if they begin throwing Dawna Polk's name and face around openly, they will be the least of the narrator's problems.
Finch admits he made a phone call and that Dawna Polk ID'd him from Courtney Polk's house, saying it is possible they were made there.
Steve says his offer extends to the people Finch has been working with and that whoever this is, they can be found and made to disappear.
The narrator responds to the offer by saying 'Points for creepy' and that the deal is 'sure as hell not going to be on those terms.'
The narrator tells Steve 'We have your phone number already—don't call us; we'll call you.'
Steve replies 'You're making a mistake,' and the narrator answers 'If I had a nickel for every time someone told me that.'
Finch and his boss watch the narrator and Arthur leave without moving from the picnic table, and their tranquility is described as unnerving.
The narrator picks up a thick, knobbly stick by the side of the pavement and throws it at the picnic area.
The butt end of the thrown branch strikes Finch's temple and then bounces off to hit Steve across the ear, and both collapse.
The narrator tells Arthur, 'Might buy us some time,' and Arthur's eyes go down to the narrator's chest and widen.
The narrator sees the bright pinpoint of a red laser sight dancing on his chest.
